title: Observer
summary: Publish events to dependents without hard-wiring their concrete classes.

body:
Rule. Observer lets subscribers register for events a subject emits. The subject knows only the subscriber interface, not concrete listeners. Use it when many modules must react to one change and you want to add listeners without editing the subject.

Why it matters. Hard-coded calls from model to UI, email, and metrics create a dependency ball. Observer inverts that: the model emits, listeners decide. Unmanaged subscriptions leak memory; mention unsubscribe in long-lived processes.

Worked example. Cart subject exposes addListener and emit item_added. UIBadgeListener increments a badge; AnalyticsListener logs; InventoryListener reserves stock. Adding EmailListener needs no Cart edit — only registration at the composition root. Sequence: cart.add(sku SKU-9); emit; each listener.handle runs. If InventoryListener throws, document whether others still run. Contrast: cart directly calling ui.refresh, analytics.track, and inventory.reserve needs an edit for every new side effect. When to use. Use observer for UI updates, in-process domain events, and metrics hooks. Use it when the set of reactors changes more often than the subject.

When to refuse. Refuse observer when there is exactly one hard-wired collaborator forever. Refuse synchronous observer chains that hide deep latency on the write path. Refuse never unsubscribing in long-lived processes. Refuse observer across network services where an explicit queue is clearer.
